clue.text: Group of bones from old Asia Minor settlement

definitions.meaning: the cluster of small bones forming the ankle and upper foot
the ancient city in Cilicia, birthplace of St Paul

explanation.definitionFit: Anatomists name the ankle bones collectively after this term, and the same word is the ancient Cilician city.

clue.text: To be severe is less than right

definitions.meaning: an illness or pain that is intense is called this
an angle smaller than ninety degrees is described this way

explanation.definitionFit: The word means intense of a pain or crisis, and in geometry describes any angle below ninety degrees.

clue.text: Boring game needs something to generate a bang

parts.note: boring, tedious, means slow
a match is a game or contest

explanation.surface: A dull sporting fixture needs some fireworks to liven it up.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow-burning fuse used to fire cannon or explosives, so it is what sets off a bang.

clue.text: Failure to hit ball means success for bowler

definitions.meaning: in baseball, a swing and a miss counts against the batter
in tenpin bowling, knocking all pins down with the first ball

explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the term is a missed swing, while in tenpin bowling it is felling every pin with one ball.

clue.text: Abandon a book, having no time to read aloud

indicators.note: having no time means a letter standing for time is dropped from the word

parts.note: to dictate is to read words aloud for someone to write down

explanation.surface: Someone gives up on a novel because they lack the hours to read it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no time' removes one T from DICTATE, leaving DICATE; this is not a homophone clue, 'to read aloud' simply means dictate.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to renounce or give up a throne or responsibility, a synonym for abandon.

clue.text: Just over 23 degrees below here? Often more

definitions.text: Just over 23 degrees below here? Often more

parts.words: Just over 23 degrees below here? Often more
parts.note: a line of latitude about 23.5 degrees from the South Pole, south of which the temperature is often more than 23 degrees below freezing

explanation.definitionFit: This parallel lies about 66.5 degrees south, roughly 23.5 degrees from the pole, in bitterly cold territory.

clue.text: Trims fish in port area

parts.note: to dock a tail or wages is to trim or cut it
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: Someone cuts up fish down at the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: The quayside region beside the docks of a harbour is the waterfront area of a port.

clue.text: Creature turned up at pound

parts.note: to turn up is to arrive, so turned up means came
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: An animal arrived at the animal pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like a reversal signal, but it simply means arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: The desert animal with one or two humps is a classic example of a creature.

clue.text: Business that's dead stuffy

parts.note: a trade whose work is literally stuffing the dead, namely preserving animal skins

explanation.definitionFit: This craft is stuffing and mounting dead animals, so its business is quite literally stuffing the dead.

clue.text: Unrestrainedly powerful new car following another vehicle with jerky movement

indicators.note: following tells us the scrambled car comes after the other vehicle

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, another word for a car

indicators.note: new signals the letters of car are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A new car trails behind another one that is lurching along.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocrat rules with absolute power, so autocratic means wielding power without restraint.

clue.text: Gnome's short or long coat

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: a gnome is a pithy saying or aphorism, so gnome is a maxim

explanation.surface: Is a garden gnome's coat short or long?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gnome' here is not a little garden figure but an old word for an aphorism.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxi is a coat or skirt reaching the ankles, the longest fashion length.

clue.text: College servant proverbially required to lie in' his work?

definitions.text: College servant proverbially required to lie in' his work?

parts.words: College servant proverbially required to lie in' his work?
parts.note: plays on the proverb 'as you make your bed, so you must lie in it', applied to a servant whose job is making beds

explanation.definitionFit: At Cambridge colleges a domestic servant who tidies students' rooms and makes their beds has this title.

clue.text: But they usually don't have appeal to young boys

definitions.text: But they usually don't have appeal to young boys

parts.note: SA is short for sex appeal
lads are young boys

explanation.surface: Lettuce and leaves rarely tempt boys.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishes of greens are classically something boys refuse, which the whole clue jokes about.

clue.text: Take a second to dock tail

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
to dock is to cut short

explanation.surface: Spend a moment cutting an animal's tail short.
explanation.definitionFit: A scut is the short upright tail of a rabbit, hare or deer.

clue.text: Set out —- a cold gale was raging

indicators.note: something raging is wild and disordered, so the letters before it are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a journey while a cold gale is blowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was raging' scrambles OUT, A, C (cold) and GALE together.
explanation.definitionFit: To coagulate is to thicken or set, as blood or custard does.

clue.text: Bound, say, to observe washing-line

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: bound means tied up
to mark is to notice or observe

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to watch for something.
explanation.definitionFit: A grubby line left round a bath or on a neck by washing, hence a line from washing.

clue.text: Wicked empress throws boy into strait

indicators.note: into tells us the boy is put inside the strait

parts.note: the Strait of Messina separates Sicily from mainland Italy
Al is a short boy's name

explanation.surface: A cruel empress hurls a lad into the sea channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Messalina, wife of Emperor Claudius, was notorious for her promiscuity and scheming.

clue.text: Sort of gold bird seen flying at pole

indicators.note: sort of here means a rearranged version of the word gold

parts.note: a lory is a brightly coloured parrot

explanation.surface: A golden bird is spotted flying near a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname of the United States flag, which is seen flying from a flagpole.

clue.text: Showing widespread sympathy as hat is blown about in wind

indicators.note: in tells us the scrambled hat goes inside the word for wind

parts.note: colic is pain from wind in the gut

indicators.note: blown about suggests the letters of hat are tossed around

explanation.surface: A hat is tossed about in a gusty wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' suggests weather, but here it is the stomach ailment; 'blown about' gives ATH, which 'in' sets inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic in its lowercase sense means broad and universal in sympathies or tastes.

clue.text: Adventurous Tom talked of this nutritious bean

indicators.note: talked of signals the name is spoken, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: Tom Sawyer is Mark Twain's adventurous boy hero

explanation.surface: Tom Sawyer spoke about a healthy bean.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the surname Sawyer is pronounced just like the bean.
explanation.definitionFit: The soya bean is a protein-rich legume widely used in food.

clue.text: Socialist designer married Iris

parts.note: orris is a kind of iris, whose root gives perfume

explanation.surface: A left-wing designer married a woman named Iris.
explanation.definitionFit: William Morris, Victorian textile and wallpaper designer, was also a prominent socialist.

clue.text: Sweet smell attracts insect

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell
a bug is an insect

explanation.surface: A sweet odour lures a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: A humbug is a hard striped peppermint boiled sweet in Britain.

clue.text: Bishop takes advantage of public transport

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to use someone is to take advantage of them

explanation.surface: A churchman exploits the bus service.
explanation.definitionFit: Buses are a common form of public transport, carrying passengers on fixed routes.

clue.text: One single party held that's worth picking out

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: held tells us the party is contained within the word for single

parts.note: sole means single or only
Lab is short for the Labour Party

explanation.surface: A lone party gathering is worth singling out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something isolable can be isolated, separated out from the rest.

clue.text: Daily failed to identify girl

indicators.note: failed suggests the word daily has broken down into a different order

explanation.surface: The daily cleaner could not recognise a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek-derived feminine given name, so it is an example of a girl, as with the youngest Bennet sister.

clue.text: Ruins the world

definitions.meaning: a planet, the red one fourth from the sun

explanation.definitionFit: To mar is to spoil, so it ruins; it is also the red planet, a world of its own.

clue.text: Playwright undisciplined in coarse play

indicators.note: in tells us the unruly word is placed within the rearranged letters
play suggests the letters of coarse are moved about freely

parts.note: wild means unruly or undisciplined

explanation.surface: An unruly actor appears in a vulgar stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like the definition's partner but scrambles the fodder to OSCARE; 'in' then sets the unruly word within it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish author of The Importance of Being Earnest was a celebrated playwright.

clue.text: Latest fashion that appears dated

definitions.meaning: a modern or current style of dress
describes dates given under the Gregorian calendar adopted in Britain in 1752

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a modern design, and historians use it to label dates reckoned by the Gregorian calendar.

clue.text: Medicine man's counterfeit article

parts.note: a sham is a fake or counterfeit
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: The healer's product is a fake.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a tribal healer and priest, often called a medicine man.
